newsitem.title: USA: Results of ballot questions and bond referendums.
newsitem.headline: Results of ballot questions and bond referendums.

text.p: The following is a list of the results of some of the November 5 ballot initiatives and measures. The list will be updated as information is made available.
P - passed. D - defeated. NA - not available
ALABAMA
NOVEMBER 5 P --Amendment No 4 - To allow for-profit bingo in Morgan County.
P --Amendment No 5 - In Jefferson County, to provide that the monetary amount of prizes for playing of bingo shall be established by local law.
P --$60 million of Mobile County, Ala., special tax bonds for bridges and drainage.
ALASKA
NOVEMBER 5
P --Ballot Measure No 1 to require popular approval or 2/3 vote of legislature to change Statehood Act.
ARIZONA
NOVEMBER 5

P --Proposition 101 - A property tax exemption for the first $50,000 of the value of personal property that is used for agriculture, trades and business. Would allow the legislature to increase the exempt amount on a national inflation index.
P --Proposition 201 - Would provide that Arizona can enter into gaming compacts with Indian Tribes that request a compact and that have not previously entered into a compact.
P --Proposition 203 - Allocate $17 million of lottery revenues annually to fund six specified health and nutrition programs.
D --Proposition 300 - Raise annual salaries of state legislators to $24,000 from $15,000.
ARKANSAS
NOVEMBER 5
NA --Amendment 1 - Establish uniform property tax rate for maintenance and operation of schools.

NA --Amendment 2 - Establish a sales/use tax of 1/8 of one percent to support the Arkansas Game and Fish Commission, the Department of Parks and Tourism, the Arkansas Department of Heritage and Keep Arkansas Beautiful.

D --Amendment 4 - Establish state lottery, bingo games and raffles by non-profit organizations and allow voters in Hot Springs to decide whether or not to authorize casino gambling at or adjacent to the Oaklawn racetrack and at two casino establishments in Hot Springs.
CALIFORNIA
NOVEMBER 5:
D --$2.4 billion Los Angeles Unified School District, Calif., school bonds.
P --$995 million, California Proposition 204 - Safe, Clean, Reliable Water Supply Act. Would authorize the issuance of general obligation bonds to finance water programs.
NA --$750 million Los Angeles, Calif., park assessment.

D --$700 million, California Proposition 205 - Youthful and Adult Offender Local Facilities Bond Act of 1996. Would authorize the issuance of general obligation bonds to construct and renovate county juvenile and adult correctional facilities.
P --$400 million, Proposition 206 - Veterans' Bond Act of 1996. Would authorize the issuance of general obligation bonds to fund a program of farm, home and mobile home loans.
P --$319 million Los Angeles County, Calif., greenbelt, zoo improvement bonds.
NA --$225 million Sacramento Unified School District, Calif., school GO bonds.
P --$100 million San Francisco, Calif., GOs.
P --Proposition 210 - Minimum Wage Increase. Increases the current state minimum wage of $4.25 per hour to $5.00 per hour on March 1, 1997 and then to $5.75 per hour on March 1, 1998.
D --Proposition 217 - Top Income Tax Brackets. Continues highest tax rates of 10 percent and 11 percent on residents with taxable income over $100,000 and $200,000 respectively.

P --Proposition 218 - Voter Approval for Local Government Taxes. Limits authority of local governments to impose taxes and property-related assessments, fees and charges. Requires majority of voters approve increases in general taxes and reiterates that two-thirds must approve special taxes.
COLORADO
NOVEMBER 5
D --Amendment 11 - Eliminates property tax exemption of churches.

P --Amendment 16 - Changes Colorado State Board of Land Commissioners' current constitutional duty of maximizing revenue from state trust lands to managing the land to produce reasonable and consistent income over time; permits the state legislature to enact laws that allow the public school fund to be used to invest in and guarantee school district bonds and to make loans to school districts.
D --Amendment 18 - Permit certain gambling in Trinidad, Colo.

D --Referendum A - Require 60 percent majority vote, instead of simple majority vote, of people to amend state constitution; provides that amendments to the constitution previously adopted with less than 60 percent of the votes may be amended or repealed until January 1, 2003, with simple majority of votes cast.
D --Referendun D - Allow unemployment insurance taxes to be increased without voter approval.
P --$100 million Colorado Springs, Colo., school bonds.
